text:

author: Swyx
text:
devin bots are multi-agent teams done right:
- always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI)
- own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others)
- manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself)
- available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction)
- consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212)

this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god)

hyped concepts this replaces:
- /goal
- "ultracode" / "ultra mode"
- "loop engineering"
- "agent to agent"
- "agent swarms"
- AI employees (see below)

my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes. 

incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol.

if youre a startup, reminder that Devin for Startups offers 65k in credits. apply via clanker

author: Josh Woodward
text:
Gemini can now do your tasks free of charge in six countries! We’ve built it for anyone who has tasks piling up during all the classes, meetings, and school drop-offs that fill the day. Our goal is for Gemini to get the job done and save you time and money along the way.

3 major updates:

1) Running on our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, Gemini can get stuff done at no cost for hundreds of millions of people across the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India.

2) Many highly requested features are rolling out now, starting in the US:
* Call local businesses (via Google Duplex)
* Pay and check out (via Google Pay)
* Text Gemini on Android or iOS (via RCS)
* Forward emails to Gemini (via Gmail)
* Sign into sites without sharing passwords outside Google (via Google Password Manager)

3) We’ve also landed our biggest update yet for the Gemini <> Google Workspace integration. The tools trigger more reliably, and you can do much more without ever leaving Gemini. Draft or send emails. Create and edit Docs or Sheets. Add multiple Calendar events at once.

Ready to hand off your next task? We can’t wait to see what Gemini crosses off your list first.

text: If you have Pro 200/500, I do recommend trying out 6.2 Sol ultrafast, it's quite the blast to use and a completely different feel. I'm excited to keep pushing in bringing these speeds to more users over time.

author: Thibault Sottiaux
text:
One of the funny reasons for the difference in vibes between the influencers and the crowd today on 6.2 Sol/Astra is that we gave a few folks access a while ago and then made a lot of changes in the last 3-4 days and I'm pretty sure no re-testing was done within those days and the videos were produced last week.

Don't get me wrong, while the models are a hefty jump compared to their GPT predecessors, they are by no means perfect and there are a few things the teams are excited for the models to get better at in future iterations in terms of taste and niceness of use. Love all the feedback and we hear you!

author: Amjad Masad
text: How scaling agent swarms can optimize software performance. https://t.co/RbOtj6u9aQ

author: Amjad Masad
text:
Agent swarms are the next scaling frontier for AI.

For years, we’ve scaled intelligence by training larger models and giving them more time to think. But there’s another dimension: running many agents in parallel, exploring different approaches, challenging each other, and working together on solutions that no single agent could easily discover.

OpenAI has already demonstrated the potential of this approach with breakthroughs in mathematics.

Until now, experimenting with agent swarms yourself required building complicated orchestration infrastructure.

Starting today on Replit, spinning up a swarm of agents is just one prompt away.

Excited to see what people discover when we make collective machine intelligence programmable by anyone.
